newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets up common property rights exchange.
newsitem.headline: China sets up common property rights exchange.

text.p: A common property rights exchange has been established along China's Yangtze River delta to enable its 10 member cities to trade idle assets, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.
The market aimed at a trade turnover of 20 billion yuan ($2.41 billion) in 1997, the newspaper said.
The 10 member cities, mostly in east China, included Shanghai, Suzhou, Wuhan and Xiamen, it said.
China had already set up a number of provincial property rights exchanges, but because they were not linked in any way, trading was dull and liquidity low, it said.
The establishment of the common market would attract more investors and provide good conditions for industrial restructuring, it said.
China now had a total of around 5,000 billion yuan in idle assets, Wednesday's Business News said.
